bitcoin wallets that cannot be hacked

in 2016 malte moser, @ittayeyal and @el33th4xor published “bitcoin vaults” and “bitcoin covenants”, describing how a simple, harmless upgrade to bitcoin script could help build hack-resistant wallets

the secret is simple: instead of attempting to build a perfect self-custody system, accept that humans are imperfect and WILL make mistakes. therefore mistakes must be recoverable

moser-eyal-sirer “vaults” add a delay to transactions. imagine if your hardware wallet had a 24 hour delay whenever sending transactions. during that delay, if you notice something is fishy (you’re getting hacked!) you hit a special button and your funds are directed to your coinbase deposit address instead, for example

that’s it! you only rely on coinbase (again, just an example) if your main wallet got hacked. if you’re not hacked, you use your wallet normally and coinbase cannot control it. you simply have to wait 24 hours when sending. for long-term storage this is usually fine

in crypto (non-bitcoin), institutional grade solutions like Safe on EVM and Squads on solana protect over $100B in assets in constructs that are similar to the 2016 vault proposal. many/most major companies in those ecosystems use those solutions and they are considered an obvious best-practice over there

but in bitcoin, this can’t be implemented without simple upgrades like OP_CTV, OP_VAULT, OP_CAT, or others

over the years, in addition to moser, eyal and sirer, many experts like @jamesob, @JeremyRubin, @kanzure, @EliBenSasson — and even retards like yours truly — have attempted to promote any of those proposals to enable this kind of safer custody. it still hasn’t been done, imo mostly due to political and puritanical reasons (various versions of “i don’t like the people who proposed this”)

but the truth is that if this feature was in bitcoin, many coldcard users would’ve been directed to use it, and would’ve been safe today. vaults and covenants don’t require wallets and humans to be perfect. they assume that they aren’t.

people who don’t want to use vaults and covenants don’t have to. but people who want to use them should be allowed to. it’s time to give bitcoiners covenants.

☢️ Uranium: The uranium market continues to send a powerful signal. The long-term uranium price is now at an all-time high, even before replacement-rate utility contracting has begun in earnest. Utilities remain under-contracted later this decade, while governments continue extending reactor lifetimes, approving new nuclear capacity and investing in domestic fuel security. If utility contracting accelerates as many market participants expect, competition for future mine supply could increase significantly.

🟠 Copper: Last week highlighted just how vulnerable supply remains. Severe winter storms disrupted mining operations in Chile, the world’s largest copper producer, reminding investors that weather is becoming an increasingly important supply risk. Combined with declining ore grades, aging mines and a shortage of new Tier 1 discoveries, the long-term supply outlook continues to tighten just as AI infrastructure, grid expansion and electrification drive higher demand.

🥈 Silver: The structural bull case remains intact. Fresnillo, the world’s largest primary silver producer, reported a 13% YoY decline in Q2 silver production due to lower ore grades. With roughly 70% of global silver produced as a byproduct, much of it from copper mines, last week’s disruptions in Chile also highlighted a potential risk to future silver supply. The market is still expected to post a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit, while AI infrastructure, data centers, power grids and electrification continue to support long-term industrial demand.

🥇 Gold: Gold remained resilient as markets balanced the Fed outlook against continued geopolitical uncertainty. Central-bank buying and persistent official-sector demand continue to provide a solid long-term foundation.

🛢️ Oil: Oil remains caught between geopolitical supply risks and uncertainty over global economic growth. OPEC+ policy and the pace of Asian demand recovery are likely to remain the key drivers in the near term.

Overall: The long-term setup for uranium, copper and silver continues to improve. Demand is rising, supply growth is becoming more difficult, and recent events only reinforce how challenging it will be to bring enough new production online in time.

Successful tokens in the future will need to do exactly two simple things:

1) Create value
2) Actually route that value back to the token somehow

That's it. Simple as that.

If you can't do that, it's questionable whether you should be building what you're building at all, and even more so whether you should be launching a token in the first place.

Everything else, and I mean the other 99% out there, is simply uninvestable and will eventually go to zero.

And honestly, that's a good thing.

We've spent years pretending that a token with no value creation and no value accrual was somehow an investment vehicle. That's over now, and people should understand that this has nothing to do with a bull or a bear market.

The market is finally maturing and starting to price this in. The tokens that create value and capture it will compound for years. The ones that do neither will bleed out, exactly as they should.

What worked for the past 10 years is not going to work for the next 10. The ones who actually want to make it should wake up to that now, or they're just wasting their time.
